name: alakazam_ml_v21
model: The v20 deck, LightGBM weights, features, confidence threshold, and guarded live scope are unchanged. v21 adds deterministic ladder-risk controls for draw, switching, promotion, attack completion, late Fezandipiti exposure, and evolution-family targeting.
model_scope: Live ML remains restricted to safe Abra/Dunsparce bench-role choice and same-evolution-card target choice. Attack, Energy, Trainer, Boss, Hammer, retreat, abilities, END, KO promotion, and effect-driven switching remain deterministic.
v21_rule_changes: Stop benched Dudunsparce draw as soon as the chosen KO route is secured, except for a narrow single-attacker continuity crisis.
Separate Abra/Dunsparce end-turn switching from post-KO promotion and price the visible next-turn KO threat.
Prefer a next-turn attacker after a KO; otherwise promote Dunsparce, Dudunsparce, then prize-clock-safe Fezandipiti ex before the Alakazam line.
Block END only when an offered attack produces real damage or counters; do not force zero-effect attacks into visible protection.
Avoid benching Fezandipiti ex at three or fewer opponent prizes unless its immediately available recovery draw creates a KO or restores offense.
Infer the opponent's important visible evolution families from card metadata and combine lineage value with prizes, energy, tools, HP, and engine text.

diagnostic_controls.ALAKAZAM_V21_TARGET_ROUTES: 1 by default; falls back to the v20 variable for compatibility
diagnostic_controls.ALAKAZAM_V21_HAND_GATE: 1 by default; falls back to the v20 variable for compatibility
diagnostic_controls.ALAKAZAM_V21_HAND_SURPLUS: 2 by default for non-Dudunsparce optional draw

known_limitations: v21 has not yet been submitted, so rating 900 or 1000 stability is not proven.
Teacher-forced replay evaluates each choice on the real v20 trajectory and cannot measure downstream states created by earlier v21 divergences.
Evolution-family targeting uses visible public card metadata; it does not claim knowledge of hidden deck contents.
The current chosen-action corpus supports pairwise candidates but is selection-biased for target ranking, so v21 does not expand live ML into Boss, attack, promotion, or switch targets.
The late Fezandipiti exception is deterministic and conservative; it does not assume favorable unknown draws beyond the guaranteed three-card hand increase.
